source: In my hometown, there is an old saying: "A distant relative is not as good as a close neighbour." When I was a child, the doors along our lane were never locked during the day. If my parents came home late from work, I would simply eat dinner at the house next door. When someone in the lane fell ill, the neighbours would take turns cooking for the family. Today most of us have moved into tall apartment buildings. We have thicker doors and better locks, yet many of us do not even know the names of the people living across the corridor.
model: 我的家乡有句老话：“远亲不如近邻。”小时候，我们那条巷子里的人家白天从不锁门。要是父母下班回来晚了，我就干脆到隔壁人家去吃晚饭。巷子里谁生了病，邻居们会轮流给这家人做饭。如今，我们大多搬进了高高的公寓楼，门更厚了，锁更好了，可许多人连住在走廊对面的人叫什么名字都不知道。

source: My grandfather kept a diary for more than sixty years. He was not a writer, and his entries were short and plain: the weather, the price of rice, who had come to visit, which tree in the yard had blossomed. As a teenager, I thought these notes were boring. Only after he passed away did I read them page by page. I suddenly realised that those ordinary sentences had recorded the history of an entire family, and that what he had left us was far more precious than money.
model: 我的祖父写了六十多年的日记。他不是作家，日记写得简短而朴素：天气如何，米价多少，谁来串过门，院子里哪棵树开了花。十几岁的时候，我觉得这些记录枯燥乏味。直到他去世以后，我才一页一页地读起来。我忽然意识到，那些平平常常的句子记录下了整个家族的历史，他留给我们的东西远比金钱珍贵。

source: Many people believe that creativity is a gift that only a few are born with. In fact, research suggests that it is more like a muscle, which grows stronger with regular use. People who are considered creative usually share a few simple habits: they stay curious about things outside their own field, they write down ideas as soon as these appear, and they are not afraid of making mistakes. As one designer put it, "If you want to have a good idea, you must first have a lot of ideas."
model: 许多人认为，创造力是少数人与生俱来的天赋。其实，研究表明，它更像肌肉，经常使用就会越来越强。被认为富有创造力的人通常有几个简单的共同习惯：他们对自己领域以外的事物保持好奇，想法一出现就立刻记下来，而且不怕犯错。正如一位设计师所说：“要想有一个好点子，你首先得有许许多多的点子。”

source: The night market is one of the liveliest places in a city. As darkness falls, stalls are set up along the street, and the air is filled with the smell of grilled meat and the shouts of vendors. Here, office workers who have just finished overtime sit next to students and tourists, sharing the same small plastic tables. For many people, a bowl of hot noodles at midnight is not only food but also comfort after a tiring day. A city without a night market, some say, is a city without warmth.
model: 夜市是一座城市里最热闹的地方之一。夜幕降临，街道两旁支起了一个个摊位，空气中弥漫着烤肉的香味和摊主的吆喝声。在这里，刚加完班的上班族与学生、游客挨着坐在一起，共用同样的小塑料桌。对许多人来说，半夜里的一碗热面不仅是食物，更是劳累一天之后的安慰。有人说，没有夜市的城市，是一座没有温度的城市。

source: When I first started learning to paint, I was eager to finish every picture as quickly as possible. My teacher, an old man with white hair, never criticised me. He only asked me to spend one whole afternoon looking at a single leaf. At first I was impatient, but gradually I noticed the tiny veins, the changing colours along the edge, and the way the light passed through it. "Painting," he told me later, "begins not with the hand but with the eye. If you have not truly seen a thing, you cannot paint it."
model: 刚开始学画的时候，我总是急着把每一幅画尽快画完。我的老师是一位白发苍苍的老人，他从不批评我，只是让我用整整一个下午去观察一片树叶。起初我很不耐烦，可渐渐地，我注意到了那些细小的叶脉、叶子边缘变化的颜色，以及光线穿过叶片的样子。后来他对我说：“画画不是从手开始的，而是从眼睛开始的。一样东西，你没有真正看见它，就画不出它。”
